/* Apply generic Luxor active-connect request failure code 10.
   
   Source:
     SoulcaliburVI.exe Ghidra analysis and live two-client invite-fallback trace
   20260714-130737-327386.
   
   Algorithm:
   1. Dereference the callback capture to recover LuxorActiveConnectPartial.
   2. Set sender/request failure code 10.
   3. Call SetLuxorActiveConnectFailedWithSenderCode, which writes state 5/substate 9 and notifies
   the active-connect queues.
   
   Parameters:
     ppActiveConnect: LuxorActiveConnectPartial ** - callback capture containing the active
   connection pointer.
   
   Returns:
     void.
   
   Rollback routing relevance:
     This function was the first state 2 to state 5 transition writer on the sandbox in trace
   20260714-130737-327386, after it received corrected opcode 0x15 traffic. The call came from a
   queued Luxor request callback, so code 10 identifies failure/expiry of the next handshake request
   rather than rejection at the endpoint send boundary.
   
   Special Cases:
     - Referenced as a callback by multiple connect-system request paths; code 10 is not yet
   assigned a narrower user-facing error name.
     - Do not infer timeout duration from this wrapper; the queueing caller owns callback timing. */

void HandleLuxorActiveConnectRequestFailureCode10(LuxorActiveConnectPartial **ppActiveConnect)

{
  uint dwSenderCode;
  
  dwSenderCode = 10;
  SetLuxorActiveConnectFailedWithSenderCode(*ppActiveConnect,&dwSenderCode);
  return;
}
